key_insight: Menopause is linked to broad blood-protein changes in inflammation, metabolism, synaptic function, and brain-aging pathways that may help explain later dementia risk.
clinical_relevance: These proteomic signals could become midlife biomarkers to identify women at higher risk for cognitive decline and to guide future prevention research.
method: Compared serum proteomics in 80 STRAW+10 staged pre-, peri-, and postmenopausal women.
Validated findings in 2,814 age-matched women using plasma Olink proteomics.
Tested whether menopause-related protein patterns related to cognitive outcomes across 4 older-women cohorts.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports replication across a larger validation cohort and consistent associations with poorer cognition in four independent cohorts totaling 11,925 women.
watch_item: Associations are observational and proteomic shifts may reflect hormonal and aging effects rather than a direct causal pathway, so clinical use needs further validation.
paper_title: Blood proteomics of menopause map to brain aging and dementia risk
